skill.name: extension-inference
skill.description: Build Caffeine canister chat features with the authenticated caffeineai-inference-client package. Use platform credentials, the router model, and secure backend-only inference calls.
skill.summary: Integrate Caffeine Inference into Motoko applications without collecting or exposing API keys.
skill.author: caffeinelabs

security_audit.summary: All 59 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, documentation links, and relative links. However, the canonical public chat endpoint lacks authorization, quotas, and rate limits, creating a high-confidence resource-abuse risk.

remediation.issue: The canonical public chat method can spend cycles and inference capacity for any caller.
remediation.suggestion: Add caller authorization, per-principal quotas, rate limits, prompt-size limits, and usage accounting to the canonical backend example.

semantic_findings.description: The canonical actor exposes chat as a public shared method without caller authorization, quotas, or rate limits. Any caller could consume inference capacity and cycles.

content.value_statement: Caffeine applications need LLM access without exposing provider keys or misconfiguring canister outcalls. This skill provides the supported authenticated Motoko integration pattern.
actual_capabilities: Adds the caffeineai-inference-client package with the documented minimum version.
Creates authenticated inference configuration from platform-provisioned runtime credentials.
Builds Motoko chat completion requests using the required router model.
Handles empty choices and missing text responses before returning content.
Explains supported chat APIs, cycle budgets, and non-streaming response behavior.
Keeps inference credentials in the backend and out of browser storage.
limitations: Supports chat completions only; embeddings, images, audio, files, and moderation APIs are unavailable.
Does not support streaming responses through management-canister HTTP.
Uses the router model and does not expose provider or model selection.
Requires Caffeine-provisioned inference credentials and a compatible Mops version.

use_cases.title: Add a Canister Chat Endpoint
use_cases.description: Create a Motoko backend method that sends prompts through Caffeine Inference and returns validated text.

use_cases.title: Review Inference Architecture
use_cases.description: Check that credentials remain backend-only and requests use supported configuration, model, and replication settings.

use_cases.title: Plan an AI Product Feature
use_cases.description: Confirm whether chat completions meet product requirements before designing frontend states and backend interfaces.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Chat
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a basic Caffeine Inference chat method to my Motoko canister. Use platform credentials and explain each changed file.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a minimal supported chat integration.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Existing Backend
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate Caffeine Inference into this existing Motoko backend. Preserve current architecture and handle empty or missing response content.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer is extending an established canister.

prompt_templates.title: Review Security and Cost Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Caffeine Inference endpoint for credential exposure, replicated outcalls, unauthorized usage, cycle costs, and missing request limits.
prompt_templates.scenario: A reviewer needs a focused deployment assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Inference Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production Caffeine Inference workflow with authorization, per-principal quotas, prompt limits, usage accounting, retries, and user-facing failure states.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced team needs operational and abuse controls.

output_examples.input: Add a summarization feature to my Caffeine application without asking users for an API key.
output_examples.output: A backend integration plan using platform credentials, a router-based chat request, validated response handling, and a simple pending frontend state.

output_examples.input: Check whether my canister inference method is ready for production.
output: Credential handling is backend-only and refreshed for each request.
Authorization, quotas, rate limits, and prompt-size limits are required before deployment.
The request must remain non-replicated and cycle usage should be monitored.

output_examples.input: Can this integration generate images and stream partial responses?
output_examples.output: No. This host supports chat completions with complete responses, not image generation or streaming.

best_practices: Create configuration from the platform environment for every request and never persist its authorization data.
Keep non-replicated outcalls enabled and use the router model for every chat completion.
Protect paid inference methods with authorization, quotas, rate limits, and bounded prompt sizes.
anti_patterns: Do not collect OpenAI keys or expose inference credentials through frontend settings, logs, queries, or actor state.
Do not call provider endpoints directly or replace platform configuration with hand-built HTTP requests.
Do not expose an unrestricted public inference method that allows anonymous callers to consume cycles.

faq.question: Do users need to provide an OpenAI API key?
faq.answer: No. Caffeine provisions inference credentials and the canister reads them at runtime.

faq.question: Which model should requests use?
faq.answer: Use the router model. The platform selects an appropriate underlying model for each request.

faq.question: Can the frontend call the inference host directly?
faq.answer: No. The frontend should call a backend canister method so credentials never reach the browser.

faq.question: Does this skill support streaming?
faq.answer: No. Management-canister HTTP returns the complete response body, so streaming must remain disabled.

faq.question: Which inference APIs are available?
faq.answer: Chat completions and the model catalog are documented. Embeddings, images, audio, files, moderation, and other OpenAI APIs are unavailable.

faq.question: What production controls should I add?
faq.answer: Add caller authorization, quotas, rate limits, prompt-size limits, usage accounting, and clear retry behavior.
